title: Additive category
statement: An *additive category* is a preadditive category $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-preadditive-category] that has a zero object and in which every two objects $A,B$ have a direct sum (biproduct) $A\oplus B$, i.e. an object with morphisms $i_A:A\to A\oplus B$, $i_B:B\to A\oplus B$, $p_A:A\oplus B\to A$, $p_B:A\oplus B\to B$ satisfying $p_Ai_A=\mathrm{id}_A$, $p_Bi_B=\mathrm{id}_B$, $p_Ai_B=0$, $p_Bi_A=0$ and $i_Ap_A+i_Bp_B=\mathrm{id}_{A\oplus B}$; equivalently, $\mathcal A$ has all finite biproducts.

source.place: Definitions 1.1-1.2, pp. 1-2 (the notion 'additive category' is used there without definition; the definition is the standard one, Stacks Definition 12.3.8)
